entries.title: Thai at a glance
body: Thai is the national language of Thailand, a Tai–Kadai language closely related to Lao. It is tonal: each syllable has one of five tones, and the tone changes the meaning.
Words never change form. There are no endings for tense, plural or gender; word order and small helper words do that work. Polite speech ends with ครับ (men) or ค่ะ (women).

examples.t: ผม{กิน}ข้าว{แล้ว}ครับ

entries.title: How Thai script works
body: Thai has 44 consonant letters and about 30 vowel forms. Vowels are written before, after, above or below the consonant they follow in speech: in เก (ke), the vowel เ is written first but said second.
Words are written without spaces between them; a space marks the end of a phrase or sentence. There are no capital letters.

examples.t: ก + า = กา · ก + ิ = กิ · เ + ก = เก · ก + ุ = กุ
examples.e: the vowel can sit after, above, before or below

examples.t: ผมชอบกินข้าวผัด
examples.e: I like to eat fried rice. (no spaces between words)

entries.title: The five tones
entries.body: Each syllable has one of five tones. The classic example is the syllable maa (or mai), which is a different word in each tone.

entries.title: Consonant classes and tone marks
body: Every consonant belongs to one of three classes: middle, high or low. The tone of a syllable comes from the class of its first consonant, whether the syllable ends in a stop (live or dead syllable), the vowel length, and any tone mark.
There are four tone marks: ่ (mai ek), ้ (mai tho), ๊ (mai tri) and ๋ (mai chattawa). The same mark gives different tones on different classes, so learn the class with each letter.

entries.title: Pronouns and polite endings
entries.body: The word for “I” depends on who is speaking and to whom. Pronouns are often dropped when the meaning is clear, and people are often addressed by their name or a kin word like พี่ (older sibling) instead of “you”.

I (woman; ดิฉัน is formal)

entries.title: Time and aspect words
entries.body: Verbs never change. These words, placed around the verb, show when something happens.

head: Word

Meaning
Example
rows: ฉันจะไป, I will go
เขากำลังกิน, he is eating
กินแล้ว, I've eaten
ยังไม่ไป, haven't gone yet

entries.title: Classifiers
entries.body: When counting, the order is noun, number, classifier. Each kind of thing has its own classifier.

entries.title: Numbers and Thai digits
entries.body: Thailand uses both Arabic digits and its own digits; prices and dates are usually in Arabic digits, but Thai digits appear on official documents and some price signs.

ไม่เผ็ดนะครับ
ห้องน้ำอยู่ที่ไหนคะ

entries.title: The wai
entries.body: The wai (ไหว้) is the Thai greeting: palms pressed together at the chest, with a slight bow. The younger or junior person wais first, and the higher the hands, the more respect. Monks are not expected to return a wai, and a shop worker's wai is usually answered with a smile or a nod.
